clue.text: Classically attractive comedian going after film role

indicators.note: the comedian is placed after the film role, coming at the end

parts.note: a picture is a film, as in 'going to the pictures'
a post is a position or job, a role in an organisation
a card is a joker, a comical person

explanation.surface: A comic lands a part in a movie, following in a long line of cinema stars.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture-postcard village is conventionally pretty, the kind of scenic view printed on holiday cards.

clue.text: Cast of soap with bold routine — ultimately, something you might see on Strictly?

definitions.text: something you might see on Strictly?
definitions.note: Strictly Come Dancing is the BBC ballroom dance contest

indicators.note: cast as in throwing or moulding the letters into a new form
the final letter of routine is used

parts.note: the last letter of the word routine

explanation.surface: A TV soap's cast perform a daring dance routine, as on Strictly Come Dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly Come Dancing is a BBC ballroom dance competition; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The paso doble is a Latin ballroom dance modelled on a bullfight, regularly performed in the competition.

clue.text: Reindeer's sweet company when the temperature drops — and safe for all

indicators.note: hot gives way to cold, so the letter for hot is swapped for the letter for cold

parts.note: Haribo is the German maker of gummy sweets
U is the film certificate meaning universal, suitable for all ages

explanation.surface: A deer's confectionery firm in a cold snap, and something everyone can enjoy safely.
explanation.walkthrough: H and C are the hot and cold tap labels, so dropping the temperature turns H into C.
explanation.definitionFit: Caribou is the North American name for the reindeer, the same Arctic species.

clue.text: Union's leader on nurses looking after heart of this poor child

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the union letter comes first
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word union

indicators.note: the nurses look after the letters by holding them inside

parts.note: the RCN is the Royal College of Nursing, the UK nurses' union

indicators.note: the middle letters of the word are taken

parts.note: the two middle letters of the word this

explanation.surface: A union boss addresses nurses caring for an impoverished child.
explanation.definitionFit: An urchin is a ragged, poorly dressed child, often a street child.

clue.text: Orgies occasionally boosted self-esteem

indicators.note: in a down clue boosted lifts the letters upwards, reading them backwards
only now and then, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of orgies

explanation.surface: Occasional wild parties gave someone a confidence lift.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is one's sense of self-worth or self-importance.

clue.text: Ring little brother up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: bro is a shortened brother; that the answer also runs backwards in the word brother is a coincidence

explanation.surface: An instruction to phone a younger sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring looks like a verb, calling the brother; it is a noun for a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: An orb is a sphere or circle, a ring-shaped or round object.

clue.text: Cross the Rubicon — initially reluctant

indicators.note: the opening letters of those words are taken

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words the and Rubicon
averse means unwilling, reluctant

explanation.surface: Caesar reluctantly crossing the Rubicon at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossing the Rubicon means passing the point of no return, after Julius Caesar's crossing of that river.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across something, synonymous with crossing it.

clue.text: 'Enhanced' man did hen do — oddly missing half of toga

indicators.note: oddly missing says the first, third, fifth letters and so on are thrown out, leaving the even ones

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: half of says the first two of the four letters are kept

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man went to a hen party, a do for brides-to-be, wearing only part of a toga: an enhanced look.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of MAN DID HEN DO give ADDED; the first half of TOGA gives TO. A hen do is a British bride's party with her friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Something added to has had more put onto it, so it has been enhanced or augmented.

clue.text: Get round as band do Auld Lang Syne last of all

indicators.note: the final letter of every word is taken

parts.note: the final letters of the five words, in order

explanation.surface: A group performs Auld Lang Syne at the very end, a way to get round something.
explanation.walkthrough: Auld Lang Syne is the Scottish song sung at New Year, often at the end of an evening.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge is to evade or circumvent something.

clue.text: Get wind of African country when making Mo Salah's first international

indicators.note: the country's opening letters are made into new ones, a replacement

parts.note: Morocco is a country in North Africa
taken as written, the first two letters of the country

indicators.note: the first letter of the footballer's surname is used

parts.note: Mo Salah is the Egyptian footballer

explanation.surface: Hearing rumours that an African nation is capping footballer Mo Salah for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: The footballer's name is split: Mo is swapped out of the country, and Salah supplies his initial in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot dusty wind blowing from North Africa across the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Discredited, forgetting I twice passed on Mastermind

indicators.note: on in an across clue says the word for passed comes after the first piece
forgetting says the letter I is dropped from the word for mastermind

parts.note: a brain is a mastermind, the clever person behind a plan

indicators.note: twice says the same letter I is dropped a second time, here from the word for passed

parts.note: passed (on, away) means died

explanation.surface: A quiz contestant is disgraced after losing the thread on Mastermind, the British TV quiz show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mastermind' looks like the quiz programme, but it is just the word for a clever person; one I is dropped from each of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Branded means marked with a stigma or bad reputation, as in branded a liar, so discredited.

clue.text: English lawyer died first — leading to post-mortem

indicators.note: the letter for died goes before the English lawyer

parts.note: a brief is British slang for a barrister or defence lawyer

explanation.surface: An English barrister has died, prompting an autopsy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface autopsy is really the after-event review of a project.
explanation.definitionFit: A debrief is a review held after an event or mission, figuratively a post-mortem on how it went.

clue.text: Florida mum's upset over vote yielding defeat

parts.note: FL is the postal code for Florida

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: mum, with the 's read as is
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
X is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A Florida mother is upset about the vote, which brings a loss.
explanation.definitionFit: To flummox is to baffle or bewilder someone, so they are beaten by the puzzle.

clue.text: Machine operator's senior going over packing area on time

indicators.note: the reversed, packed word follows on after the time letter
the reversed senior packs the area letter inside it
going over, as if flipped, means the word is turned backwards

parts.note: an elder is one's senior

explanation.surface: A senior figure inspects the workers boxing goods in an area, keeping to schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot-pedal lever that drives a machine such as an old sewing machine or lathe.

clue.text: Items papers used in place of hard news

indicators.note: the papers take the place of the hard letter

parts.note: items are things
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Newspapers carried the items rather than hard news.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings is an old-fashioned word for news or information.

clue.text: Somehow he sees us double number

definitions.note: a number is a song, here a rock and roll classic

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters get there in some unspecified way, mixed up

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer wonders how a man is seeing double of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Number is a song, as in a musical number, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue Suede Shoes is the Carl Perkins rock and roll song made famous by Elvis Presley.

clue.text: See 14
Exclude damaged Easter egg

indicators.note: a damaged egg is broken, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave out a broken chocolate egg.
explanation.definitionFit: To segregate is to separate people or things and keep them apart.

clue.text: It could be 18 Across to begin with — set it around motorway

indicators.note: the start of the word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word across
to gel is to set, like a jelly

indicators.note: the word it goes around the motorway

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: It might be 18 Across, an engagement ring, at first, set around a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The 18 Across reference is a decoy: 18 is the number, and Across just supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eighteen is a common minimum age, as for drinking or voting, set as an age limit.

clue.text: Band that shows promise getting buzz after gig

indicators.note: the buzz comes after the gig

parts.note: a gig or booking for a performer is an engagement
to give someone a buzz is to ring them on the phone

explanation.surface: A promising pop group gets an excited reaction following a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: Band and gig suggest music; the band is a finger ring and the promise is to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: An engagement ring is worn to show a promise of marriage.

clue.text: Frisks group of doctors during strike in recession

indicators.note: receding means going back, so everything is read in reverse
the doctors come during the strike, inside it

parts.note: to slog is to hit hard, strike
the BMA is the British Medical Association

explanation.surface: Doctors' union members are searched during industrial action in an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: Frisks and strike suggest police and industrial action; frisks here means leaps playfully.
explanation.definitionFit: To gambol is to skip and leap about playfully, like a lamb.

clue.text: See 18
No reason to start blaze

indicators.note: the reasoning goes first, with the word no after it

parts.note: to reason is to infer, deduce

explanation.surface: There was no motive for starting the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a large, fierce fire.

clue.text: One of five content to leave cheese and fruit

parts.note: a quin is a quintuplet, one of five born together

indicators.note: the contents of the word leave, keeping only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of cheese, with the middle gone

explanation.surface: A quintuplet happily abandons cheese and fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The quince is a hard, aromatic pear-shaped fruit used for jelly.

clue.text: Difficult politician left former partner's business at the outset

indicators.note: the business letters are placed at the very beginning

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
an MP is a Member of Parliament
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A politician quit a firm that belonged to an ex-spouse at the start, and it was awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Complex means complicated, intricate and hard to deal with.

clue.text: Ape shot outside Malawi's capital

indicators.note: the shot goes outside the letter, around it

parts.note: a chip is a short lofted shot in golf or football

indicators.note: the capital letter, the first one, of the word

parts.note: the initial of the country Malawi

explanation.surface: A great ape is shot near Lilongwe, Malawi's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital suggests the city; it means the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimp, short for chimpanzee, is one of the great apes.

clue.text: Posh females splitting fish dish

indicators.note: the posh females split the fish by sitting inside it

parts.note: the sole is a flatfish
U means upper-class, a British usage for posh
F is the abbreviation for female, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Upper-class women share out a fish course between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A souffle is a light baked dish made with whipped egg whites, savoury or sweet.

clue.text: Club having staff for event

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
to staff something is to man it

explanation.surface: A golf club employs people for a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ironman is a gruelling triathlon race of swimming, cycling and running, a sporting competition.

clue.text: New phone company is born

parts.note: EE is a UK mobile phone network

explanation.surface: A new telecoms firm has come into being.
explanation.definitionFit: Nee is used before a woman's maiden name, meaning born with that surname.

clue.text: Crooned revolutionary song — it's punchy

parts.note: to croon is to sing softly, so crooned is sang

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: Someone sang a rebel anthem with a lot of force.
explanation.walkthrough: Punchy here means being a punch, the drink, not forceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine mixed with fruit, so it is the drink in question.

clue.text: Child star on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio things are heard, not seen, so the word is spoken

parts.note: the sun is a star

explanation.surface: A child celebrity broadcasting on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A son is a male child of his parents.

clue.text: He helps to even up supply and exceed normal limits

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone assists in levelling out the provision of goods, and goes above and beyond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun; it is the adverb from supple, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To push the envelope is an idiom from test flying for going beyond accepted boundaries.
